corpus_role: extraction stress — icon-font glyph corruption lands on every contact field; heavy ORG false-positive surface
extraction_notes: This resume uses an icon font (FontAwesome or similar) for contact-line markers. Every icon extracts as a junk character, and every one is adjacent to a PII field. This is the single most realistic extraction-failure document in the corpus — LaTeX/Overleaf resume templates do this constantly.
'I (123) 456-7890' — leading 'I' is a corrupted phone icon.
'# alfred.pennyworth@email.com' — leading '#' is a corrupted envelope icon.
'1/22020 – Present' — page-number '1/2' fused to the year '2020'.
Trailing '2/2' page marker at end of document.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Preceded by a stray 'I' glyph with a space. Regex should still match the number itself; the risk is upstream — if the deconstructor treats 'I (123) 456-7890' as a non-contact field because it fails a format check, the whole line may be routed to free text instead of the contact block, bypassing tier 0.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Preceded by '# '. A regex using a permissive local-part character class may capture '#' into the match; one anchored on a word boundary will not. Either way it must be suppressed — but if the harness compares matched strings exactly, a '#'-inclusive match scores as a miss against this label. Recommend scoring on span overlap, not string equality.

known_traps: Icon-font glyph corruption adjacent to ALL FOUR contact fields — the defining feature of this document. If tier 0 field routing depends on clean contact-line formatting, this document breaks it.
ap-006 / ap-007 — bare social handles whose only identifying marker was the icon that failed to extract. Expect a miss; documents that icon fonts must be handled at the PDF layer.
ap-023 / ap-022 — institution names containing LOCATION substrings. Tests ORG/LOCATION boundary handling; failure produces visibly corrupted output.
ap-002 'Silicon Valley' — colloquial region absent from most gazetteers.
Eight distinct work/education LOCATIONs — the densest location test in the corpus.
Five FAANG ORG names as negative controls for PERSON detection, plus 'Amazon' and 'Apple' as LOCATION/common-noun risks.
